automation_classes.procedural: Deterministic code. Same inputs give the same output; no model in the loop.
automation_classes.algorithmic-search: A measured loop: change a parameter, measure, keep the better value. Needs a metric, not judgement.
automation_classes.local-model: A local vision or language model can do it well enough, with a numeric check afterwards.
automation_classes.frontier-model: Needs a frontier multimodal model (or a person): spatial reasoning from a picture into 3D code, new motion design, or diagnosing why a render is wrong.
automation_classes.human: A person decides: taste, approval, publication.

stages.title: Reference painting
stages.check: A person approves the identity art.
stages.why: Image generation or hand art. Style consistency across a roster is a judgement; a local image model can draft but drifts from the house style.

stages.title: Part-built model and base rig
inputs: an existing species builder to start from
stages.check: Silhouette review beside the reference from front, three-quarter and back.
stages.why: Turning a 2D character into proportioned 3D forms is spatial design. Out of scope for this workflow's code, which starts from a built model.

stages.title: Sample pigment colours from the reference
inputs: named sample points or cluster count
outputs: colours as sRGB hex with spread
stages.check: Spread (standard deviation) of each sample is small; clusters cover the painting.
stages.why: Median of a pixel window and k-means are exact. Choosing which region each colour belongs to is the next stage.

stages.title: Author markings as functions of position
inputs: part names and positions from the builder
outputs: painter(T) in the consumer's markings file
stages.check: compare-palette numbers, then a look at the review sheet for placement.
stages.why: The reference is a posed 2D picture and the model has different proportions, so every marking must be re-placed relative to model landmarks (a brow above this model's eye, not at the painting's pixel). A local vision model can name the markings; placing them in 3D coordinates and writing the masks took spatial reasoning plus two or three visual iterations per animal.

stages.title: Bake the painted atlas and embed it
stages.check: validate-glb: every material textured, UVs inside the atlas.
stages.why: Charts, packing, rasterising, pigment wash and contact pooling are deterministic.

stages.title: Engine material and lighting calibration
inputs: review render in the real scene
outputs: shader constants (light, shadow band, fill, ambient)
stages.check: compare-palette: dominant pigments within about +/-15 per 8-bit channel on screen.
stages.why: Once the shader has the right terms, tuning the constants against the palette metric is a search. Finding the terms the first time was diagnosis: albedo applied twice by the existing light function, a sky ambient that lit tops far more than fronts, and tonemap saturation. Do not trust a model's visual impression of brightness; in this project it read a face as bright gold that measured mid-tan. Measure.

stages.title: Add bone chains for tails, trunks, manes, wings
stages.why: Bones laid along the same path the tube sweeps, weights blended across joints: no judgement once the archetype says a chain is wanted.

stages.title: Clips from an existing archetype
outputs: Idle, Walk or Fly, Greet clips
stages.check: clip report: loops close, slide near 0 at the game's speed, nothing below the floor, no pops.
stages.why: Choosing numbers for an existing routine (how sleepy, how bouncy, which arm waves) is parameter filling that a local model can do, because the clip report catches bad values. The stride is derived from the game's speed, not chosen.

stages.title: New motion or a new archetype
stages.check: clip report plus pose sheet and motion preview review.
stages.why: A crawl, a trunk that trumpets, wings that trail: these were designed, not looked up. Recorded reference video plus ArcoreAnimate's tracking is the alternative route for motion that should look captured rather than authored.
tools: ArcoreAnimate (video to rig) for captured motion

stages.title: Numeric clip review
outputs: per clip: length, loop gap, implied ground speed, foot slide, lowest point, pops
stages.why: Reads the file and runs the skeleton forward. This found foot skating and sinking paws that stills and previews did not show.

stages.title: In-engine review captures
inputs: consumer capture scripts in the real scene
stages.check: Captures exist for every animal and clip.
stages.why: Scripted. The scene and the flow that brings the character on screen are the game's, so the capture scripts are consumer adapters.

stages.title: Does it look right and move right
outputs: list of fixes or approval to continue
stages.check: Each finding is tied to a capture or a number.
stages.why: Marking placement, silhouette reading and whether a walk reads as that animal are judgements. A local vision model is useful for presence checks (is there a tail stripe) but missed placement and motion quality; pair any model's opinion with the numbers.

stages.title: Game-readiness check
outputs: issues with severity; stats: clips, bones, textures, triangles

stages.title: Consumer gameplay tests
stages.check: All pass from source; packaged build re-tested before release.

stages.title: Archive source and runtime files
stages.check: Stored checksums equal local files; status stays review.
